chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from one who informed him, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them):

Regarding the witnesses: if they testify against a man and then retract their testimony after a judgment has been rendered against the man, they are liable for what they testified to and are fined; but if judgment has not yet been rendered, their testimony is discarded and the witnesses are not fined anything.
ai.seo_question: What are the legal consequences for witnesses who retract their testimony after a court judgment has been issued?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *daman* (liability) for witnesses who retract their testimony after a judgment has been rendered, ensuring they bear the financial consequences of their error. It contrasts this with pre-judgment retraction, where testimony is merely discarded without penalty, reflecting the juristic focus on the finality of judicial decisions in Shia fiqh. This ruling underscores the seriousness of testimony as a binding legal instrument once the court has acted upon it.
